name: Iqbâlî (Sultan Mustafa II)
bio: Mustafa II succeeded his uncle Ahmed II in 1695 and led his army against the Austrians; he wrote verse under the pen-name Iqbali.
The poems here are taken from E. J. W. Gibb's Ottoman Poems (1882), the first English verse translations of Ottoman poetry; dates and biographical details follow Gibb's Biographical Notices.

poems.title: Allah! Lord Who Livest for Aye
poems.author: Iqbâlî (Sultan Mustafa II)
poems.text:
Allah! Lord who livest for aye! O Sole! O King of Glory's Ray!
Monarch who ne'er shalt pass away! show Thou to us Thy bounties fair.

In early morning shall our cry, our wail, mount to Thy Throne on high:
"Error and sin our wont," we sigh: show Thou to us Thy bounties fair.

If cometh not from Thee Thy grace, evil shall all our works deface;
O Lord of Being and of Space! show Thou to us Thy bounties fair.

Creator of security! to Thy Beloved greetings be!
These words are in sincerity: show Thou to us Thy bounties fair.

Iqbâlî sinned hath indeed, yet unto him Thy grace concede;
Eternal, Answerer in need! show Thou to us Thy bounties fair.
